provenance: CodeVetter local Go benchmark over deterministic stub providers; no database, network, external-provider, production-load, or user-latency claim.

flow_progression.boundary: Exclusions were caller skips. The earlier pre-sized-map verifier is evidence for one source hypothesis, not proof that every later finding at that source is rejected.

static_catalog_experiment.candidate: Precompute deterministic catalog logo URLs in the existing immutable search index.
static_catalog_experiment.memory_boundary: One RSS repeat moved 8.957% and 16.9 MiB, below the conjunctive 10% plus 16 MiB rejection gate; the other repeats moved 2.44% and 2.026%. RSS remains a noisy regression guard, not retained-memory attribution.

candidate_key_progression.result: One candidate-key exclusion suppressed the later live-search finding and advanced the lab to the no-match flow without mutating either diagnosis.

context_candidate_key_progression.result: An unrelated fund-analysis source edit changed snapshot and finding identity while preserving the selected-function digest and candidate key. The existing exclusion still suppressed the source during the complete current-snapshot replay.

sparse_catalog_allocation_experiment.candidate: Delay queryful catalog result capacity until the first match while preserving full no-query preallocation.
sparse_catalog_allocation_experiment.claim_boundary: The no-query path retains its original full-limit preallocation and existing initial-dropdown correctness coverage. Results remain local stub-backed evidence.

fund_delta_allocation_experiment.candidate: Retain scalar return deltas while ranking and expose pointers only from final winner storage.
fund_delta_allocation_experiment.post_change_profile: The changed function had no remaining direct eligible allocation finding; only non-experiment-eligible cumulative callers remained.
fund_delta_allocation_experiment.claim_boundary: The benchmark is deterministic in-process fixture analysis. It excludes database, provider, request, production-load, and user-latency effects.

post_fix_flow_coverage.boundary: All discovered safe local benchmark flows were measured on one snapshot. Four earlier source candidates remained caller-excluded; this does not verify them as rejected and does not establish production coverage.

tooling_followup.previous_selection: The first diagnosis spent bounded source slots on several pprof lines from eodhdResultToItem and selected its 17.16% direct map-allocation row; the map-capacity experiment was rejected.
tooling_followup.corrected_selection: Source contexts are now deduplicated by file and function. A Polaris-shaped replay selects forLogoDevTicker at 6.86% direct object share because its one-line literal-plus-%s fmt.Sprintf pattern is concrete, while still returning only one unverified experiment candidate whose argument types require checking.
tooling_followup.unsupported_boundary: Dynamic, numeric, width, precision, cumulative-only, and sub-5% sources do not receive this preference.
tooling_followup.cross_flow_progression: Finding exclusions now project into coverage. A candidate-exhausted flow remains visible and measured but yields to the next safe unmeasured flow; terminal exhaustion remains explicit when no safe action remains.
tooling_followup.candidate_key_progression: New source findings bind their opaque candidate key to the bounded selected function digest and stable source/mechanism identity. Unrelated edits and line movement preserve the key; selected-function edits invalidate it. Legacy snapshot-bound findings remain readable.

limitations: Go pprof allocation values are normalized per operation and do not represent retained heap or peak memory.
The profile attribution inventory hit its bound; complete benchmark metrics remain authoritative for the paired comparison.
Peak RSS is sampled from the owned benchmark binary and is a regression guard, not source attribution.
The result is local deterministic evidence and does not establish production impact.
